newsitem.title: UK: Blair's first 100 days -- a chronology.
newsitem.headline: Blair's first 100 days -- a chronology.

text.p: Tony Blair has swept like a whirlwind through British politics since the May 1 election which catapulted him to power with a huge 179-seat majority.
The following is a summary of the first 100 days in power of Britain's first Labour Prime Minister since 1979.
MAY 2 - Blair enters Downing Street as prime minister, starts naming cabinet of 17 men and five women.
MAY 6 - Finance minister Chancellor Gordon Brown raises interest rates by 1/4 point and stuns financiers by giving the Bank of England power to set rates in future.
MAY 11 -- Ministry of Defence delights veterans by promising substantial new resources to investigate Gulf War Syndrome.
MAY 12 - Robin Cook issues Foreign Office's mission statement, putting human rights at heart of his agenda.
MAY 14 -- Queen's Speech maps out radical programme for next 18 months comprising at least 22 bills. Heading the programme are plans for separate parliaments for Scotland and Wales.
MAY 16 -- Blair launches new peace initiative in Belfast, inviting Sinn Fein to talks with government officials.
MAY 19 -- Health Secretary Frank Dobson says government will ban tobacco firms' sponsorship of sport as well as advertising.
MAY 21 -- Government promises to destroy all British anti-personnel landmines by 2005, and ban their import, export and manufacture.
MAY 28 -- Government reaffirms determination to hand national lottery to a profit-free operator after directors of organisers Camelot award themselves big pay increases.
MAY 29 -- Blair's meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton wins rave reviews after two leaders crown start of a new special relationship by unveiling joint G7 jobs initiative.
JUNE 5 -- First opinion poll since the election gives Blair a record-high 82 percent approval rating.
JUNE 16 - Blair breaks off contacts with Sinn Fein after IRA murders two policemen, the "darkest" day of his premiership so far.
JUNE 17 -- Blair, in Amsterdam for his first EU summit, claims a triumph for preserving control of Britain's borders, thwarting plans for a European army and putting jobs on agenda.
JUNE 20-22 -- Blair, at his first G7 summit, enlists Clinton's support in drive for peace in Northern Ireland and says his crusade for flexible labour markets is making headway.

JUNE 25 -- Blair announces new proposals designed to allow Sinn Fein to enter peace talks in Northern Ireland under which decommissioning of guerrilla weapons can proceed in tandem with all-party talks on the province's future.
JUNE 30 -- Blair attends Hong Kong handover ceremonies, says he wants a strong and stable relationship with China.

JULY 2 -- Brown's first budget kicks off welfare-to-work programme by taxing windfall profits of privatised utilities. Labour MPs pleased by extra funds for health and education. Economists fear he has not done enough to slow consumer demand.
JULY 6 -- Violence erupts in Northern Ireland as police give go ahead to controversial pro-British Protestant march through a Catholic enclave in Portadown.
JULY 15 -- Mad cow disease rears its head again as government is forced to tighten checks on illegal beef exports after furore over beef smuggling allegations.
JULY 17 -- Government confirms 1999 European Parliament elections will be by proportional representation.
Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman launches biggest review of pensions since World War Two.
JULY 19 -- IRA says it will begin ceasefire at noon on July 20. But Ulster Unionists threaten to boycott peace talks without cast-iron assurances on weapons disarmament.

JULY 22 -- Blair announces consultative cabinet committee with Liberal Democrats to discuss areas of mutual interest such as constitutional affairs, a move hailed as first step toward reconfiguration of centre-left of British politics.
International Monetary Fund, in a glowing report, says Labour has made an excellent start in its economic policies.
JULY 28 - Government unveils plans for powerful new Mayor for London plus capital's first city-wide representative body since 1986.
JULY 31 - Government announces new code of conduct for ministers to prevent repeat of sleaze which affected previous Conservative administration.
AUGUST 1 - Conservatives win first by-election of new parliament, at Uxbridge, west London, with an increased majority from May election.
